# Windows Forms Designer

Windows Forms apps are typically built using the Visual Studio drag-and-drop Designer, which generates C# (or VB) code — not markup — describing the form's controls and layout in a paired `.Designer.cs` file.

## Signature / Usage

```csharp
// MyForm.Designer.cs (generated by the Designer)
partial class MyForm
{
    private System.ComponentModel.IContainer components = null;
    private Button okButton;

    private void InitializeComponent()
    {
        this.okButton = new Button();
        this.okButton.Text = "OK";
        this.okButton.Location = new System.Drawing.Point(150, 120);
        this.okButton.Click += new System.EventHandler(this.okButton_Click);

        this.Controls.Add(this.okButton);
        this.Text = "MyForm";
    }
}
```

```csharp
// MyForm.cs (your code, partial class pair)
public partial class MyForm : Form
{
    public MyForm()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    private void okButton_Click(object sender, EventArgs e) { /* ... */ }
}
```

## Options / Props

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `.Designer.cs` | Generated partial class containing `InitializeComponent()`; do not edit by hand (Designer round-trips this file) |
| `InitializeComponent()` | Called from the form's constructor; creates and configures all controls |
| `FlowLayoutPanel` / `TableLayoutPanel` / `SplitContainer` | Layout containers usable inside the Designer |
| Data Sources window | Drag-and-drop data binding from databases/web services/objects onto forms |
| `UserControl` | Base class for authoring custom reusable controls in the Designer |

## Notes

- Unlike WPF/XAML, there is no markup language — the Designer's output is imperative C#/VB code that instantiates and configures `Control` objects.
- The .NET (non-.NET-Framework) Windows Forms Designer requires Visual Studio; some newer .NET Windows Forms projects may have partial or evolving Designer support depending on the Visual Studio version — check current tooling support before assuming parity with .NET Framework WinForms.
- WPF has no direct Designer equivalent for markup generation (its XAML Designer edits markup directly, not generated code); WinUI 3 currently has no Design view at all (Hot Reload only).
